title: Enterprise Onboarding 1 Support Process, Escalation Playbook, Health Checks & QBR Template
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary
-------
This document is the canonical playbook for enterprise onboarding and post-go-live support with Redwood Inference. It consolidates the recommended support process, the escalation playbook, integration checklist, known issues and workarounds, and the Health Check / QBR template used by Customer Success (CS) and Support teams for customers on Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. Use this as the single source of truth during onboarding, escalation handling, and quarterly reviews.

Scope and applicability
----------------------
- Applies to: Enterprise customers (Dedicated and Private, and high-volume Hosted customers)
- Teams: Customer Success, Support, Solutions Engineering, Product Reliability, SRE, Sales Engineering
- Phases covered: Pre-onboarding checklist, onboarding induction, integration, go-live, post-go-live support, escalations, health checks, and QBRs

Ownership and roles
-------------------
- Customer Success (owner): overall onboarding plan, QBRs, success milestones
- Support (owner): triage, ticketing, first-line troubleshooting, SLA adherence
- Solutions Engineering: integration guidance, test plan, runbook handover
- SRE / Eng-Platform: incident response for platform issues, service-level diagnostics
- Account Executive / Sales: contract, legal/PO, and billing handover

Prerequisites before onboarding start
-----------------------------------
1) Signed contract + SOW with named contacts and billing info.
2) Access & security: customer-provided allowlist IPs, KMS/HSM requirements (if Private), and legal privacy terms finalized.
3) Technical readiness: test dataset sample, expected QPS, peak concurrency, average sequence length, and representative prompts.
4) Network connectivity test: egress rules and TLS termination details.

Pre-Onboarding checklist (to be completed by CS + SE)
----------------------------------------------------
1. Kickoff scheduled (agenda attached below) 1 include technical and business stakeholders.
2. Share integration guide and API key provisioning steps.
3. Confirm environment: Hosted / Dedicated pool ID / Private deployment cluster details.
4. Validate network/firewall rules: allowlist whitelisted IPs or FQDNs and required ports (443).
5. Prepare test prompts and success metrics (latency, cost-per-token targets, quality gates).
6. Assign runbook owners and support rotation.

Kickoff agenda (30160 minutes)
-----------------------------
- Introductions and roles (5 min)
- Goals, success metrics, and timeline (10 min)
- Integration approach: API vs SDK vs Private (10 min)
- Security, compliance, and data flows (10 min)
- Next steps and immediate action items (510 min)

Integration guide 1 key items (short summary)
-------------------------------------------
- API / SDK access
  - Provisioning: CS requests API keys via internal portal; keys scoped to project and rotation policy (90 days).
  - Example curl: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <KEY>' -d '{"model":"rwd-llama-2-13b", "input":"Hello"}'
- Network / egress
  - Allowlist: customers should allow outbound to api.redwood.example (A records documented in onboarding packet).
  - Private: provide CIDR ranges and VPN/BGP details; confirm KMS access.
- Rate limits & capacity
  - Hosted: per-account rate limits documented in the customer portal.
  - Dedicated: reserved GPU pool; document burst capacity and autoscale policies in the Dedicated SOW.
- Observability hooks
  - Customer to install tracing headers, report sample request IDs for debugging; provide example logging payloads.
- Test plan
  - Step 1: smoke tests (auth, basic generation)
  - Step 2: perf tests (P95 latency, throughput at target QPS)
  - Step 3: quality tests (sample prompts + expected outputs)

Onboarding runbook (numbered steps)
----------------------------------
1. CS: Kickoff & collect technical contacts, share packet.
2. SE: Provision API key / Dedicated pool access and confirm connectivity.
3. Customer: Run smoke tests and share logs for any failures.
4. SE: Perform perf tests during agreed window and record baselines.
5. CS + Customer: Verify quality gates against evaluation prompts.
6. SE / Eng-SRE: Validate monitoring (dashboards, alerts) and set up alert notifications to the support channel.
7. Go/No-Go meeting: confirm SLOs and operate in canary mode for 48172 hours before full production traffic.

Support process & SLAs
----------------------
- Channels: Zendesk (ticketing), Slack (customer-specific channel for live escalations), email, and phone for high-severity incidents.
- Ticket intake workflow: Customer -> Zendesk -> Support triage -> Assign to SE/SRE if needed -> Escalate per playbook.
- SLA targets (enterprise):
  - P1 (platform down, customer-facing outage): initial response 15 minutes, update cadence 30 minutes until mitigation, resolution target 24 hours (varies by root cause).
  - P2 (degraded performance, partial outage): initial response 1 hour, update cadence 4 hours, resolution target 72 hours.
  - P3 (feature request or minor issue): initial response 8 business hours, resolution per roadmap/patch schedule.
- Escalation ownership table (single-line format)
  - Support Tier 1: Support oncall 1 triage and recreate.
  - Support Tier 2: Solutions Engineering 1 integration issues and config changes.
  - Support Tier 3: Eng-SRE / Runtime team 1 kernel/runtime, capacity, or infrastructure faults.

Escalation playbook (P1 example)
--------------------------------
1. Detection: Alert from monitoring or customer-reported ticket.
2. Triage (Support Tier 1): Confirm customer impact, collect request IDs, timestamps, and sample payloads.
3. Notify oncall and open incident in PagerDuty with severity=P1.
4. Initial mitigation: revert recent config/model rollout if indicated; enable fallback model variant per routing policy.
5. Engage Eng-SRE: provide collected artifacts (logs, pprof snapshots, KV cache stats).
6. Communication: CS owns customer communications; Support provides technical updates every 30 minutes.
7. Post-incident: complete incident review and action items assigned in 72 hours.

Known issues and workarounds (live examples)
-------------------------------------------
| ID | Symptom | Scope | Workaround | Status |
|----|---------|-------|-----------|--------|
| KI-2026-001 | Intermittent 503s for high-concurrency Dedicated pools | Dedicated (burst autoscale path) | Reduce client concurrency or enable queued requests; escalate to Eng-SRE to inspect autoscaler logs | active |
| KI-2026-002 | Elevated P95 latency when average prompt length > 1024 tokens | Hosted & Dedicated | Use prefix/KV caching and shorten system prompt; enable quantization profile optimized for long sequences | monitoring |
| KI-2026-003 | Embeddings endpoint returns inconsistent vector dims after model swap | Hosted | Recreate client session and fetch model metadata endpoint before request; coordinate model swap during low-traffic window | resolved |

Note: Add new KIs to the Known Issues tracker with steps to reproduce, customer impact, and mitigation timeline.

Health checks & QBR template
---------------------------
Purpose: Regular cadence to ensure the customer's usage is healthy, cost is predictable, and quality/regressions are detected early. Use the template below for monthly health checks and quarterly business reviews (QBRs).

Monthly health check checklist
- Availability (last 30d): API success rate > 99.95%
- Latency (last 30d): P95 < customer SLA target (documented per account)
- Error budget usage: % of error budget consumed this period
- Cost per 1k tokens: baseline vs current trend
- Model quality: % prompts failing quality gate (from eval suite)
- Open tickets: count and avg time to resolution
- Capacity headroom: Baseline vs peak 95th percentile usage

QBR agenda (60190 minutes)
1. Executive summary (510 min): adoption, value delivered, key wins
2. Operational review (15120 min): availability, latency, SLO adherence, incidents since last QBR
3. Cost & efficiency (15 min): unit economics, recommended batching/quantization changes, Dedicated sizing discussion
4. Product roadmap & feature requests (1015 min)
5. Risks & mitigations (10 min): security, capacity, compliance items
6. Action items & owners (510 min)

QBR deliverables (post-meeting)
- Updated health dashboard snapshot (PDF link)
- Action item tracker with owners and due dates
- Follow-up plan for model/ops changes and expected impact

Templates & sample messages
---------------------------
- Go-live confirmation (email): brief template confirming success criteria met and production cutover times.
- P1 customer update cadence (Slack/email): timestamps and short status lines.
- QBR invite template with pre-read materials requested.

Post-incident review & continuous improvement
-------------------------------------------
- All P1/P2 incidents require an Incident Review within 72 hours.
- Reviews must capture: timeline, root cause, mitigation, owners for action items, and regression tests added to eval harness.
- Track recurring issues in the Reliability Initiatives board; prioritize fixes in the roadmap.
